label: EXPLAINED_ABSENCE_2: an absence fixed by the admissibility constraints or by a carried exclusion
definition: PositivelyFixedAbsence Admissible RequiresLack Has x k: either no admissible profile contains all of x's real determinations together with k (case i or ii of #2153: the admissibility constraints, alone or with x's positive profile, exclude k), or some real determination t of x requires the lack of a set S that contains k and whose other members x has (a carried exclusion, the sense of carriage LE). It is the sense of 'explained' that 'no unexplained absence at roots' (9281317d) uses. It is not 'some reason for the absence is admitted' (EXPLAINED_ABSENCE_1): a bare negative clause in a nature is an admitted reason in the #755 arena and fixes nothing here. Under the necessity direction of member grounding (89c988d9) the second disjunct implies the first (carriedClosureNotUnexplained), so the sense reduces to case (i) or (ii).
note: Stipulated for #2145 lane H2 (docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section on inquiry and closure at the root). Examples: a root's lack of an impure limiter that no admissible profile contains (case i); a lack of k carried by a determination that requires the lack of k. Non-example: the lack of noesis at a source whose nature contains the bare clause 'lacks noesis' and whose profile with noesis added is admissible: it has an admitted reason (the clause) and is not positively fixed. The definition introduces no new primitive; it composes HasCompatibleExtension, ActualProfile and the primitive RequiresLack of RootPerfectionIntellect. What would source it: a source stating that every negation at a simple being is grounded in what it positively is; none is attributed.
